harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Joined node2's and node3's segments (attached to node1's eth1 and eth2 respectively) into a single L2 domain via a Linux bridge (br0) on node1, with STP off. node2 (ens7) and node3 (ens7) were assigned 192.168.50.11/24 and 192.168.50.12/24 in the same subnet, persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-ens7.cfg. node1's br0 has no IP address and performs pure frame forwarding rather than routing, confirmed by matching ICMP TTL=64 (unchanged) and ARP tables on node2/node3 showing each other's real MAC addresses directly (not node1's). Bridge setup was made persistent across reboot via a new systemd unit (l2-bridge.service) enabled at boot on node1, since SONiC's interfaces-config.service only manages eth0 and does not conflict. Segment mapping (eth1->node2, eth2->node3) was empirically confirmed via targeted tcpdump capture during broadcast pings before wiring the bridge. All three nodes were then restarted one at a time (node2, then node3, then node1 last since it disrupts both segments), each showing a changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id post-restart, and full bridge/connectivity recovery was verified afterward (bridge forwarding state, br0 addressless, and successful bidirectional ping node2<->node3 with ARP entries showing direct peer MACs).
actions_performed: Inspected node1/node2/node3 network state (ip addr, ip route, docker ps) to establish baseline topology
Identified eth1/eth2 on node1 as bridge uplinks to node2/node3's ens7 via targeted tcpdump capture during broadcast ping tests
Cleaned up docker0's stray class-E IP and flushed eth1/eth2 addresses on node1
Created br0 bridge on node1 with eth1 and eth2 as members, STP disabled
Assigned 192.168.50.11/24 and 192.168.50.12/24 to node2 and node3's ens7 interfaces
Verified transparent L2 forwarding via unchanged ICMP TTL and direct-peer ARP entries (not node1's MAC)
Persisted bridge config via new systemd unit /etc/systemd/system/l2-bridge.service enabled at boot on node1
Persisted node2/node3 ens7 IPs via /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-ens7.cfg (ifupdown, Ubuntu 16.04)
Captured healthy baseline (boot_id, bridge state, ping) on all three nodes
Restarted node2, node3, then node1 sequentially via 'sudo reboot', polling each until exec access returned
Verified changed boot_id and full recovery (bridge forwarding state, addressless br0, node2<->node3 ping and ARP) after each restart

evidence.requirement: Baseline healthy state before any restart (bridge built, connectivity working)
evidence.summary: br0 bridge created with eth1/eth2 forwarding, ping node2<->node3 succeeds, ARP tables show direct peer MACs (transparent L2, not routed), boot_ids captured pre-restart

evidence.requirement: Segment mapping (which node1 NIC maps to which peer) determined empirically, not assumed
evidence.summary: tcpdump on eth1/eth2 during node2's broadcast ping showed the 192.168.50.x traffic arriving only on eth1, confirming eth1->node2, eth2->node3

evidence.requirement: Persistence of bridge config across reboot (node1)
evidence.summary: Created and enabled /etc/systemd/system/l2-bridge.service (WantedBy multi-user.target and sonic.target) running /usr/local/sbin/l2-bridge-setup.sh

evidence.requirement: Persistence of IP config across reboot (node2, node3)
evidence.summary: Wrote /etc/network/interfaces.d/60-ens7.cfg on both nodes with static 192.168.50.11/12 addresses

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged (connection closed), boot_id changed from 35c87ec9 to 75267425, post-restart ens7 IP persisted and ping to node3 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged (connection closed), boot_id changed from a9593011 to 92c2d8c9, post-restart ens7 IP persisted and ping to node2 succeeded

evidence.requirement: node1 restart: acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered state (bridge, cluster function)
evidence.summary: Reboot acknowledged before disconnect, boot_id changed from 6cef3db6 to 2dc313d8, l2-bridge.service ran successfully at boot recreating br0 with eth1/eth2 forwarding and no IP on br0

evidence.requirement: Final end-to-end verification that the L2 domain and transparent forwarding survived all restarts
evidence.summary: node2->node3 ping succeeds post all-node restart; node3's ARP table shows node2's real MAC directly, confirming node1 still forwards frames transparently rather than routing
